LESSON: SELF- IMPROVEMENT

Grade: Grade 8
Subject: SOCIAL STUDIES
Strand: Social Studies and Personal Management Self-Improvement 4 Self- Esteem Assessmen
Topic 1.1: Self- Improvement

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Self- Improvement. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: Which animal best reflects your personal characteristics?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. describe personality traits for self- understanding
2. share goals for self- improvement in social life
3. appreciate the role of values in the development of personality traits

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: SELF- IMPROVEMENT
Subject: SOCIAL STUDIES · Grade: Grade 8
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Self- Improvement helps you succeed in SOCIAL STUDIES. You will understand it, practise it, and use it in your county, school, and Kenyan community.

KEY FACTS: SELF- IMPROVEMENT
Good citizens follow rules, respect others, and care for shared places.
Kenyan examples: lining up, keeping the compound clean, telling the truth, helping a classmate.
Rights come with responsibilities.

PART 1: Describe personality traits for self- understanding

What this means
In this part you learn to describe personality traits for self- understanding. You will use ideas from in your county, school, and Kenyan community.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: describe personality traits for self- understanding.
2. Locate, explain, then act responsibly using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Locate: Connect “Self- Improvement” to a real place or group in Kenya (school, market, county office, home).

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can describe personality traits for self- understanding. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Share goals for self- improvement in social life

What this means
In this part you learn to share goals for self- improvement in social life. You will use ideas from in your county, school, and Kenyan community.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: share goals for self- improvement in social life.
2. Locate, explain, then act responsibly using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Explain: Give one cause and one effect linked to Self- Improvement.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can share goals for self- improvement in social life. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 3: Appreciate the role of values in the development of personality traits

What this means
In this part you learn to appreciate the role of values in the development of personality traits. You will use ideas from in your county, school, and Kenyan community.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: appreciate the role of values in the development of personality traits.
2. Locate, explain, then act responsibly using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Participate: Describe one responsible action a Grade learner can take.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can appreciate the role of values in the development of personality traits. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Self- Improvement is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Good citizens follow rules, respect others, and care for shared places.

Kenyan examples: lining up, keeping the compound clean, telling the truth, helping a classmate.

Example 1: Connect “Self- Improvement” to a real place or group in Kenya (school, market, county office, home). (skill: describe personality traits for self- understanding)

Example 2: Give one cause and one effect linked to Self- Improvement. (skill: share goals for self- improvement in social life)

Example 3: Describe one responsible action a Grade learner can take. (skill: appreciate the role of values in the development of personality traits)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Self- Improvement to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: describe personality traits for self- understanding.
3. Practise this skill: share goals for self- improvement in social life.
4. Practise this skill: appreciate the role of values in the development of personality traits.
5. Make one local Kenya example of Self- Improvement from your county, market, farm, or school.
6. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Self- Improvement: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 8 learner study Self- Improvement?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. Which animal best reflects your personal characteristics?
2. What career choices in Social Studies relate to you?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Self- Improvement means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: describe personality traits for self- understanding.
5. Be able to: share goals for self- improvement in social life.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
